title: Sunscreen SPF50

drivers.name: 30% off promotion (deeper than past)
drivers.evidence: Past promotions: median lift x1.02 (noise-adjusted), max x1.68 (10% off). This is 30% off—deeper than any seen. 2025-09-08: 30% off, x1.26. TikTok trend adds momentum. No prior 30% off with viral signal.

drivers.name: TikTok trend (new driver)
drivers.evidence: Product trending on TikTok with no prior promotion. Not captured in historical uplift model. Suggests potential for viral demand spike beyond past promotion patterns. No similar event in history.

adjustment.analysis: The 30% off promotion is deeper than past promotions (max 25% off), and the product trended on TikTok with no prior promotion, suggesting stronger lift. The baseline is already adjusting for seasonal decline (trend -21.9% over 13 weeks), so no additional trend adjustment. Past promotions show median lift x1.02, but this is a deeper discount and viral context. The classical model underestimates due to lack of viral signal. Noise-adjusted lift from past promotions is x1.02, but we shrink toward 1.0 only with thin evidence—here, the TikTok trend and deeper discount justify a higher multiplier. No overlapping events. Downside spread unchanged (no risk).

  median 24.9 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 64.6 | 10%-90%: 1.6 - 44.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
